name: Tute individual
description: Tute for two players; no partnerships. Standard 40-card Spanish deck. Ten cards each, stock with face-up trump; follow suit and overtake; Cantes (40/20) after winning a trick; Tute (4 Kings or 4 Knights) wins the deal. Most points in the deal wins that game; session is multiple deals.

overview.description: Tute for two players; no partnerships. Standard 40-card Spanish deck. Ten cards each, stock with face-up trump; follow suit and overtake; Cantes (40/20) after winning a trick; Tute (4 Kings or 4 Knights) wins the deal. Most points in the deal wins that game; session is multiple deals.

history.origins: Originated in Italy (as tutti); spread to Spain in the 19th century where it became one of the most popular card games. Two-player individual variant.
timeline: 19th century: Tute spread from Italy to Spain; two-player individual variant became widely played.

setup.deck: Standard Spanish pack of 40 cards: four suits (Swords/espadas, Batons/bastos, Cups/copas, Coins/oros). Ranks and point values: Ace 11, Three 10, King 4, Horse 3, Jack 2; Seven through Two count zero. One suit is trump each deal, determined by the face-up card.
setup.dealing: 10 each, next card face up for trump, remainder as stock; after each trick winner draws first then others anticlockwise.

rules.objective: Score the most points in the deal (card points, Cantes, last trick). Follow suit and overtake when possible; trump if void. Declare 40 or 20 after winning a trick; Tute (4 Kings or 4 Knights) wins the deal outright.
rules.gameplay: Dealer deals 10 cards each; next card is trump, rest form stock. Player to dealer's right leads. Follow suit; must beat led suit if possible; if void must trump if possible. Trick winner draws first from stock, then opponent. After winning a trick you may declare one Cante (King+Horse of same suit: 40 in trumps, 20 in other). Declaring Tute (all four Kings or all four Horses) wins the deal. Last trick scores 10 extra. Most points wins the deal.
keyRules: Follow suit and overtake; trump when void
Cantes 40/20 after winning trick; Tute wins deal

scoring.winCondition: Most points in the deal wins (card points, Cantes, last trick 10). Tute (4 Kings or 4 Knights) declared after winning a trick wins the deal outright.

synthesis.shortDescription: Tute for two players; no partnerships. Same 40-card Spanish deck, Cantes, Tute (4 Kings/4 Knights). First to 101 points wins.
